title: Choose the Casino Pass 2.0 direction
question: All three keep the QR code permanently visible, scale proportionally to the phone, and leave the current pass untouched. Pick the structure that should become the interactive beta.

options.label: Casino Cage Ledger
options.lineage: casino cage plaques and serialized gaming ledgers
options.thesis: A precision credential that feels issued from the casino cage, with every field accounted for and the QR protected as the validation seal.
options.viewport: One tall proportional pass fills the phone: event marque at top, guest ledger through the middle, and a large white QR bay anchored at the bottom.
options.risk: Its precision can feel formal unless the responsive brass details and tactile press states keep it alive.

options.label: Playing Card Reveal
options.lineage: oversized court cards and casino table reveals
options.thesis: The guest becomes the face card: identity, event and access form one dramatic composition while the scan zone remains fixed and untouched.
options.viewport: A near-full-screen court card holds the guest portrait hierarchy above a high-contrast QR panel; tilt reveals foil registration without moving the code.
options.risk: The court-card metaphor must stay disciplined so identity and admission details never become ornamental.

options.label: Royal Flush Ticket
options.lineage: premium casino admission tickets and live-table markers
options.thesis: A bold scan-first ticket with the energy of the casino floor and the speed of a modern mobile boarding pass.
options.viewport: The event title and guest name sit above an oversized central QR code, with date, venue and raffle balance compressed into one clear footer rail.
options.risk: It is the most immediately usable direction, but also the closest to a familiar digital-ticket pattern.
